title: Atlys Launches Visa Support Services to Help Indian Travelers Before and After Rejection
excerpt: The travel tech startup introduces Atlys Assure, which covers flight and hotel costs up to ₹5 lakh if a strong application is still rejected, and Rejection Recovery, which helps travelers understand refusal reasons and rebuild their case.
body:
• Atlys has launched two visa services: Assure, which assesses applications before submission and covers travel costs up to ₹5 lakh if a strong application is rejected, and Rejection Recovery, which helps applicants understand refusal reasons and prepare a fresh case
  • Rejected Indian visa applications cost applicants an estimated ₹662 crore in application fees alone in 2024, with Schengen rejections adding another ₹155 crore in 2025
  • Atlys Assure is available for eight visa markets including Schengen, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, China, Japan and South Korea, at no additional charge
  • The services come amid stricter visa scrutiny globally, including expanded US social-media screening that has triggered a surge in 221(g) administrative processing notices for Indian applicants

Indian travelers applying for visas to popular destinations face an expensive gamble. A rejection means lost application fees, and often lost money on flights and hotels booked in anticipation of approval. Atlys, the travel technology startup founded by Mohak Nahta, is now trying to address both sides of that problem with two new services — Atlys Assure and Rejection Recovery.

The Scale of the Problem

The financial cost of visa rejections for Indian applicants is substantial. In 2024, rejected visitor visa applications are estimated to have cost Indian applicants around ₹662 crore in application fees alone. European Commission data for 2025 shows that more than 1.81 lakh Indian Schengen applications were rejected, with roughly ₹155 crore spent on fees that did not lead to a visa.

Those figures do not include the cost of cancelled flights, hotel bookings and holiday plans — expenses that often run into lakhs per family.

How Atlys Assure Works

Atlys Assure steps in before a traveler submits a visa application. The service assesses the application and compares the case against Atlys's own approval history to estimate the chances of success. If the application appears weak, travelers are told what could be improved before they commit money to flights and accommodation.

For applications that Atlys considers highly likely to succeed, there is an additional layer of protection: if the visa is still rejected, Atlys will cover booked flight and hotel costs up to ₹5 lakh per application. There is no separate charge for the Assure service — it is included with the application.

Assure is currently available for eight visa markets: Schengen countries, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, China, Japan and South Korea.

Rejection Recovery

For travelers who have already been refused a visa — including those who applied independently or through another service — Rejection Recovery offers a structured path back. The traveler uploads their rejection letter, and Atlys explains the reasons in simpler language, breaking down terms such as US Section 214(b) or Schengen Article 32.

The application is then assessed across areas such as financial strength and ties to the home country. Atlys specialists help rebuild the application, followed by a structured week-by-week plan for reapplication.

"At Atlys, we're always trying to take friction out of the visa journey. Travellers need clearer answers before they spend money, and practical help after something goes wrong." — Mohak Nahta, Founder and CEO of Atlys

A Tougher Visa Landscape

The services arrive at a moment of heightened visa scrutiny for Indian applicants globally. The US State Department expanded social-media vetting for all temporary-visa classes in late 2025, and Indian applicants have reported a sharp jump in 221(g) notices — effectively administrative processing delays — at US consular posts. Consular officers now review up to five years of social media activity on platforms including Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and GitHub.

China's new two-stage pre-approval system, introduced in late December 2025, has pushed rejection rates for Indian applicants to nearly 40 per cent, according to industry estimates. The UK, Canada and Schengen countries have also tightened documentation requirements.

For diaspora families coordinating visits by relatives from India, these rejection rates and the associated costs create real friction. Services that reduce the financial risk and provide clearer guidance on refusal reasons could help streamline a process that has become increasingly opaque and expensive.

Atlys also offers a separate service called Atlys Protect, which refunds the visa application fee itself if the application is rejected — distinct from Assure's coverage of travel booking costs.
nri_angle: Relevant to diaspora families coordinating visits by relatives from India who face rising visa rejection rates and steep financial costs.
